info.title: CAS
info.description: The passkey identity provider of MemeBattle: the JSON API under `/api` for its own frontend, and the OpenID Connect endpoints at the root. Every error response lists the stable codes it can carry in `x-error-codes`; clients branch on those codes, never on messages.

post.summary:
Ends the session the cookie names and clears the cookie. Idempotent and
never a 401: a browser holding an expired or already revoked cookie is
asking to forget it, and the answer to that is yes.
post.description:
The removal cookie stays even though `Clear-Site-Data` asks for the
cookies as well: a browser that does not implement the header — and it is
not universal — has only the removal cookie to go on, and the two say the
same thing.

204.description: Signed out; the cookie is cleared whether or not a session was ended.

Set-Cookie.description: The removal of the session cookie (`Max-Age=0`).

patch.description:

absent email is a `204` like any other. Nothing is returned; the
dashboard reads the account back through `GET /api/me`.

get.summary: The authorization endpoint: the authorization code flow with PKCE.
get.description:
The parameters are those of OpenID Connect Core §3.1.2.1 in the query:
`client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `response_type=code`, `scope` with `openid`,
`state`, `code_challenge` with `code_challenge_method=S256`, and
optionally `nonce`, `prompt=none` and `id_token_hint`; they are read by
hand under the RFC's rules, a repeated one refused (ADR 0010, ADR 0015).
Before the client and its redirect URI are known the answer is CAS's
page; after, every answer is a redirect.

302.description: To the client's redirect URI with `code` and `state`, or with `error`, `error_description` and `state` (`x-error-codes` lists the `error` values); or, without a signed-in session, to the frontend's `/sign-in` or, for a guest upgrade, `/create-account` with `return_to`.

Set-Cookie.description: An upgrade session for a guest's `id_token_hint` (ADR 0015).

get.summary: RP-initiated logout, the parameters in the query.
get.description:
`id_token_hint` (required, an ID token CAS issued to the client,
expired or not), `client_id`, `post_logout_redirect_uri` and `state`
(RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 §2), read by hand, a repeated one refused. The
session the cookie names is ended only when it is the hint's account's
(ADR 0013).

post.summary:
The token endpoint: the authorization code exchange, the refresh, and
the guest grant.
post.description:
The body is `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (RFC 6749 §3.2), read
by hand under the RFC's rules, a repeated parameter refused:
`grant_type=authorization_code` with `code`, `redirect_uri` and
`code_verifier` (ADR 0011); `grant_type=refresh_token` with
`refresh_token` and an optional `scope` (ADR 0012);
`grant_type=urn:memebattle:oauth:grant-type:guest` with an optional
`scope` (ADR 0014). A confidential client authenticates with
`Authorization: Basic` or with `client_id` and `client_secret` in the
body, a public client sends `client_id` alone. Every answer is
`Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`.

AccountType.description:
Whether an account has credentials of its own.

Maps to the Postgres `account_type` enum; on the wire it is the same
lowercase word.

registrationId.description: Identifies the ceremony; the client brings it back to finish.

Discovery.description:
The discovery document. It advertises the whole SSO milestone, including
the endpoints later tickets add, so that it stays the same across their
releases (ADR 0009 (f)).

request_uri_parameter_supported.description:
Discovery §3 defaults this to `true`, and `/authorize` refuses
`request_uri` (ADR 0010 (b)), so it is stated. The sibling
`request_parameter_supported` defaults to `false` and stays implicit.

token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported.description:
`none` is a public client, which authenticates with its `client_id`
and proves itself with PKCE (OpenID Connect Core §9, ADR 0011).

Jwks.description: A JWK Set: the body of `/jwks.json`.

loginId.description: Identifies the ceremony; the client brings it back to finish.

MeResponse.description:
The signed-in account as the dashboard needs it. Nothing about the
session itself but when it ends if left alone: the id is server-side
state.

email.description: `null` when the account has no address.

PasskeyResponse.description:
A passkey as the dashboard shows it. The credential itself (public key,
counter, flags) is server-side state and never leaves.

lastUsedAt.description: `null` until the passkey is first used to sign in.

PublicJwk.description:
The public half of a signing key, as `/jwks.json` publishes it
(RFC 7517, RFC 7518 §6.2.1).

displayName.description:
Validated by the handler rather than by the type, so a bad name gets
its own error code instead of a generic `invalid_body`.

registrationId.description:
Identifies the ceremony; the client brings it back to finish. Not the
account id, which only a finished registration reveals.

name.description:
Validated by the handler rather than by the type, so a bad name gets
its own error code instead of a generic `invalid_body`.

TokenResponse.description:
The tokens, RFC 6749 §5.1 and OpenID Connect Core §3.1.3.3.

The fields are in alphabetical order, the order the members had when the
body was built as a JSON map, so the bytes on the wire did not change.

access_token.description: An ES256 JWT (RFC 9068) for the client's resource server.

email.description:
`null` clears the address. The field is required: with the serde
default a missing key would read as `null` and clear the address a
client never mentioned. Validated by the handler rather than by the
type, so a bad address gets its own error code.

UserInfoClaims.description:
The `/userinfo` answer (OpenID Connect Core §5.3.2): `sub` and
`account_type` always, the rest as the token's scopes release it — never
a `name` for a guest. `iss`,
`aud` and `amr` are the ID token's business and are not repeated; Core
requires only `sub`.

VerifyLoginResponse.description:
Who signed in and with which credential. A session (#667) will accompany
this; until then the client learns the account id and nothing else.

VerifyRegistrationResponse.description:
What the client needs after a successful registration: who it now is, and
which credential was stored. The credential itself is server-side state and
is never sent back.

basic.description: `client_secret_basic`: a confidential client's id and secret.

session.name: cas_session
session.description: The session cookie set by registration and login (ADR 0004). On an https origin its name is `__Host-cas_session`.
